$comment: The fixed probe set for G8. These queries are NEVER changed casually:
their whole value is that the same questions get asked of every build, so
a shift in results means the DATA changed, not the question. Adding a
probe is fine; editing or removing one invalidates the baseline and must
be done in a PR that says why.
Chosen to span the failure modes we actually fear: broad queries that
could turn to mush as data accumulates, narrow queries that could get
buried by it, and adversarial near-misses that should NOT match.
2026-07-30: OT probes added. Layer B grew from Psalms-only to 99% of the
Bible while every probe still sat in Psalms and the New Testament, so the
gate could not see the material that changed most. These probe the genres
the OT expositors actually cover — law, narrative, histories, wisdom,
prophecy — against fixture chapters added for the purpose.

probes.query: be doers of the word not hearers only
built his house on the rock
a very present help in trouble

probes.why: No scriptural content. If accumulated data ever makes this return matches, weak signals have started firing on nothing.
Pure stopwords. Must produce no tokens and therefore no results, no matter how much data is admitted.
Law. Exodus 20 is dense legal register; should surface the commandment, not every occurrence of 'not'.
Law. Leviticus 19:18 is the OT root of a heavily-quoted NT phrase — tests that the OT source is not buried by NT restatements.

probes.query: the LORD bless you and keep you
probes.why: Liturgy. Numbers was the least-covered book before Keil & Delitzsch; this is its most-quoted passage.

probes.query: where you go I will go
probes.why: Narrative. Ruth 1:16 — tests that narrative speech is retrievable, a genre absent from the fixture until now.
Histories. 1 Kings 19 — strong imagery in a genre commentators treat unevenly.

probes.query: if my people who are called by my name humble themselves
probes.why: Histories. 2 Chronicles 7:14. Chronicles sat at 32% coverage before KD; this verifies the new evidence surfaces.

probes.query: trust in the LORD with all your heart
probes.why: Wisdom. Proverbs 3:5 — sapiential register, distinct vocabulary from law and prophecy.
Wisdom. Ecclesiastes 3 — repetitive structure that could easily turn to mush as term profiles accumulate.

probes.query: he was pierced for our transgressions
probes.why: Prophecy. Isaiah 53 — heavily expounded, so a good test of whether volume of commentary distorts ranking.

probes.query: thoughts of peace and not of evil
probes.why: Prophecy. Jeremiah 29:11 in the WEB's own wording. The familiar 'plans to prosper you' is NIV phrasing and appears nowhere in this corpus — a real product gap recorded in NEEDS-JESSE, not something a probe can paper over. Probes must ask questions the corpus can answer, or they measure the question rather than the data.

probes.query: do justly love mercy walk humbly
probes.why: Minor prophets. Micah 6:8 — a genre with no coverage at all before this round.

Genealogical register, targeting Genesis 5 which the fixture carries. List-material has almost no distinctive theological vocabulary, so this watches for the failure mode where accumulated commentary makes genealogy match thematic queries across the canon.
